short: A program that can take steps on its own — calling tools, reading files, sending emails — instead of only answering a question.
body: Agents differ from chatbots in one thing: they act. A chatbot drafts an email; an agent can open your CRM, find the deal, write the email and log the result. That autonomy is why they need guardrails.

short: A large language model: a model trained on massive amounts of text that predicts the next token.
body: The same architecture behind ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. What changed recently is not the basic idea but the tool use, context length and reliability around it.

short: The unit a model reads and writes — roughly three quarters of an English word.
body: Pricing is quoted per token, so a 3,000-word document is roughly 4,000 input tokens. Output usually costs more than input.

short: How much a model can hold in mind at once — the prompt, files and conversation.
body: When a task needs more than the window, you must summarise or retrieve. This is the single most common cause of agents forgetting instructions.

short: Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant documents, then let the model answer using them.
body: It is how you make an answer cite your own documents instead of the model's training data. It reduces hallucinations but does not remove them.

short: A list of numbers that represents the meaning of a piece of text.
body: Embeddings let you search by meaning rather than keywords — the basis of vector search and semantic retrieval.

short: Storage optimised for searching embeddings.
body: It answers "which of my 50,000 chunks is closest to this question?" quickly. For small collections, a plain database with an index is often enough.

short: A rule that blocks or redirects an unsafe or off-target action.
body: Guardrails are checks around the model: validate the input, constrain the tools it can call, and validate the output before it reaches a customer.

short: Letting a model call an external function — a search, a calculator, an API.
body: It is the difference between an assistant that describes and one that acts. The cost is that errors become actions, so tool calls need validation.

short: The protocol that lets a model request a specific function with structured arguments.
body: The model does not run the function; it asks your application to, then reads the result back. You are always in control of execution.

short: Model Context Protocol: an open standard for connecting models to tools and data sources.
body: Adopting it means a tool written once works across many AI applications instead of being re-implemented per vendor.

short: Designing instructions so a model produces the output you need, reliably.
body: Most of the gain comes from clarity, examples and explicit output formats. Prompt stuffing and clever tricks age badly.

short: Getting the model to return data in a fixed shape, such as JSON.
body: It removes most parsing work. The cost is the model occasionally breaking the schema, so validate before you trust it.

short: A confident, fluent answer that is not supported by the facts.
body: It happens because the model predicts plausible text, not verified truth. Retrieval, citations and validation reduce it; nothing eliminates it.

short: Training an existing model further on your own examples.
body: Worth it when the format is stable and you have hundreds of good examples. For most teams, better retrieval and a better prompt are cheaper and faster.

short: The layer that decides which agent or tool runs, and in what order.
body: It is the difference between a demo and a system. Orchestration owns retries, timeouts, budgets and what happens when a step fails.

short: Moving data between apps without a human touching it.
body: Tools like n8n, Make and Zapier are workflow engines: they trigger on an event, run steps and move data. They are not the same thing as an agent.

short: An open-source workflow automation tool you can self-host.
body: You write the steps in nodes, and you can drop into JavaScript when a node is not enough. That is why it survives contact with real data.

short: A visual automation platform with a generous free tier.
body: Good for teams without developers. The trade-off is that complex scenarios become large visual scenarios.

short: The oldest and largest Zap-hub automation service.
body: Its app catalogue is unmatched, and so is its pricing on heavy usage. If a task is unusual, expect a step that is slower than the alternatives.

short: A library that handles the loop of model, tools, memory and retries.
body: LangChain, CrewAI and LangGraph are the common choices. Frameworks speed up the prototype and slow down the odd case — know when to drop to plain code.

short: A step where a person approves before the system acts.
body: The cheapest insurance for anything that touches money, customers or legal commitments. High-value, low-frequency tasks should always have one.

short: Seeing what the system actually did — traces, costs, retries, failures.
body: Without traces, an agent failure is a story. With them, it is a line in a log: which prompt, which tool, which argument.

short: What one unit of work costs and earns.
body: For a tool with per-seat pricing, revenue per customer divided by service cost per customer tells you whether growth is worth funding.

short: Customer acquisition cost: what you spend to win one customer.
body: Divide total sales and marketing spend by new customers in the period. Compare it to gross margin, not to revenue.

short: Lifetime value: the gross profit a customer generates before they leave.
body: A rough version is average monthly gross profit times average lifetime in months. A LTV:CAC below 3x usually means growth is buying losses.

short: The multiplier you apply to cost to get a price.
body: Cost 10, sell 30 is a 3x markup and a 66% margin. Confusing the two is the most common pricing mistake.

short: Profit as a percentage of the selling price.
body: It is the number that survives contact with tax, fees and shipping. Compute margin after costs, never before.

short: The revenue where costs equal income.
body: Fixed costs divided by contribution margin gives the sales volume you need before the business stops losing money.

short: Value added tax charged on consumption in most of the EU and many other countries.
body: Rates, thresholds and registration rules differ per country, so a "global" VAT rate does not exist. Check your local rules before quoting a customer.

short: Goods and services tax, used in Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Singapore.
body: It is the VAT equivalent in those markets, with the same practical question: who is registered, and what happens below the threshold.

short: The amount that lands in your account after tax and social security.
body: Gross pay minus income tax and national insurance or FICA. It is the number that matters for every budget decision.

short: The hourly rate that makes your freelancing sustainable.
body: Divide your annual target by billable hours, then add 25–40% for the cost of being your own employer. Most people underprice by half.

short: Software delivered over the internet on a subscription.
body: The pricing model is the risk: per-seat costs scale with headcount, and per-usage costs scale with the very growth you want.

short: The rate at which customers stop paying.
body: For a small team, five customers leaving can erase a quarter of revenue. Churn is the first number to watch, not new sales.

short: Selling to businesses versus to individuals.
body: B2B has longer cycles, higher contract values and a real need for a human relationship. B2C has volume and almost no tolerance for friction.

short: The system where a company tracks prospects and customers.
body: A CRM is only useful if someone owns the data quality. Automating a dirty CRM just automates the mess.

short: Ranking prospects by how likely they are to buy.
body: Score on fit and behaviour, not just company size. A scoring model nobody trusts gets ignored, and then it is worthless.

short: An HTTP callback fired when something happens in another system.
body: Webhooks are how tools talk in real time. Polling works but wastes requests and adds latency.

short: A programmatic interface a product exposes to other software.
body: APIs are how you automate anything a product does not offer in its own UI. Check rate limits and error handling before you depend on one.

short: The cap on how many requests an API accepts in a period.
body: Rate limits shape architecture: batch requests, cache aggressively, and make the workflow resumable rather than retrying blindly.

short: The property that repeating an operation does not duplicate its effect.
body: It matters whenever a workflow can be retried — charges, emails, record creation. Pass an idempotency key and the second attempt becomes a no-op.

short: Single sign-on that lets staff log in with one identity.
body: It removes password resets and offboarding leaks. It also adds setup work and, for small teams, a vendor that sells it as a feature.

short: An independent security attestation for a SaaS provider.
body: It is what enterprise buyers ask for first. It is also expensive and slow, so for a small team, hosting choices often matter more.

short: Building data minimisation into the product, not bolting it on.
body: Decide what you do not need to collect. Data you never store cannot leak, cannot be subpoenaed and does not need to be deleted.
